requirements.text: create a replacement unit at the same customer location
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM installed_product WHERE installed_product_id = 301 AND account_id = 33 AND product_id = 140 AND location_id = 867 AND status = 'in_use'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (301 after 300); the only row the task creates in this table, and the benchmark's case checks point at 301

the unit replaced is installed product 182 (P140-411674-6934, Phillips-Jones, account 33, location 867): of the four in_use P140- units it ties unit 42 on open case load (3 each) and alone carries a critical open case (747), so business impact decides before the warranty tie-break

unit 42 is nearer its warranty boundary (2026-12-20) but Stark Industries holds no active warranty contract (23 is draft, 138 expired), so it fails 'if the warranty is still valid'; of the two warranty-valid units (113, 182), 182 is closer to its boundary

warranty valid for 182: contract 82 (warranty, active, to 2027-03-19) with active entitlement 295 for product 140; the unit's own warranty_end 2027-09-16 is after the seed's latest timestamp (2026-06-24)
same product (140) and location (867) as the old unit, per 'keeping product details ... consistent'; status in_use because the policy requires installed products to be active / in_use
serial_number and warranty_end are not fixed by the request or policy and are not tested

disagreement: cells: A adds serial_number LIKE 'P140-%' (every seed unit follows 'P<product_id>-...'), B does not; dropped because the pattern is a seed convention, not a rule of the request or policy, and a replacement unit carries its own serial

notes: Merged from two passes that agree on the unit (182 replaced by 301), on all eleven requirements' rows and on all seven dispositions (kept). disagreement: value: the new unit's serial, A tests serial_number LIKE 'P140-%', B does not; dropped because nothing in the request or policy fixes the replacement's serial (logged on the requirement). disagreement: value: the three case updates, A tests installed_product_id = 301 only, B also product_id = 140; kept B's as the tighter right form, backed by the policy's product-match rule and by the seed (all three cases carry 140 already). disagreement: form: the notification rows, A selects by case with email as a cell, B repeats case, email and type in selector and cells; written with the natural key (case and recipient) as selector and type as the cell, same SQL. The benchmark never checks the replacement unit's own row, only the cases pointing at id 301; requirement 1 adds it. The unit choice rests on reading 'warranty still valid' through the contract table (the policy says repair and replacement commitments depend on warranty contracts); under the unit's own warranty_end alone, unit 42 (2026-12-20) would still be valid and is the one nearest its boundary, so an agent reading it that way would pick 42 and fail every check here. The acting user (32, Jose Roberson) is an admin whose user row is inactive (active = 0); the policy says nothing about inactive actors and tells the assistant to assume admin responsibilities, so no requirement follows from it. register_new_installed_product, update_installed_product_details, update_case and send_notification cover every written table.
